messages:
Joel K: follow-up to the escrow sketch. I've been thinking about bounded buffers and eviction policies if frontdoors start hoarding escrows during global retry storms. propose a small sized LRU-ish ring per-instance + a tenant-priority fast-path.

Priya R: LRU per-instance makes sense to limit memory, but how do we avoid unfair evictions for high-priority tenants?

Joel K: plan: keep two rings: one for normal escrows, one for protected tenants (customer flag). protected ring has reservation slots. eviction order: normal LRU -> probation -> protected LRU only after abnormally high pressure and explicit policy override.

Sam T: sounds complicated but doable. eviction event should emit a soft-deny signal to admission so clients see a 429 instead of silent reclaim. we should avoid silent charge reclamations for paid customers.

Lina (SRE): ops concern: cross-region routing. If a tenant hits frontdoor A and places escrow, then client gets routed to frontdoor B which has no view, they might be rejected even though quota exists. Need clear semantics: escrow is non-authoritative. admission has to validate real balance before accepting a dispatch commit.

Joel K: yes. escrow only reduces the chance of double-debit at ingress. admission remains source-of-truth for long-term accounting. commit flow: 1) frontdoor escrow claim, 2) admission validate+persist debit, 3) frontdoor commit ack to client. if admission cannot validate, frontdoor reclaims escrow and return appropriate error.

Priya R: what about batching commits to admission? that could reduce load but increase risk window for double-charges if admission fails between batch intervals.

Sam T: tradeoff: batch interval vs double-charge risk. suggestion: allow per-tenant commit_mode: immediate, micro-batch (100ms), or deferred (for low-priority bursty workloads). default hosted -> micro-batch 50ms. Dedicated -> immediate.

Lina (SRE): monitoring must show escrow_latency, batch_commit_size, uncommitted_escrow_bytes. alert on uncommitted_escrow_bytes > threshold for > 1m. Also a clear runbook: if the uncommitted buffer grows, roll traffic away from affected frontdoor instance.

Joel K: eviction policy sketch:

```
per_instance_capacity: 5000
protected_reservation: 500
eviction_order:
  - normal: lru
  - probation: oldest_flagged
  - protected: lru_when_overflow
```

Priya R: abuse heuristics we can run at escrow time: excessive idempotency reuse, token-hopping across tenants, short-lived idempotency keys with many attempts. flagged escrows go to probation ring with stricter commit checks.

Sam T: billing reconciliation: need a reconciliation job that scans escrows that were committed vs those reclaimed and correct any off-by-one in billing pipeline. add an escrow_audit_id to every commit event.

Lina (SRE): operational feature: health endpoint /escrow/metrics that returns counts per-instance + top-k tenants holding escrows (useful for on-call debugging). must be read-only and gated behind admin auth.

infra-bot: rollout note: enabling protected_reservation requires both frontdoor and admission schema bump. plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 10m observation windows. link: https://go/redwood/escrow-rollout

Joel K: UX: we should expose per-tenant policy flags in console: escrow_enabled, commit_mode, protected_reservation. defaults: hosted: escrow_enabled=true, commit_mode=micro-batch; dedicated: escrow_enabled=false, commit_mode=immediate.

Priya R: one more edge: streaming sessions should not hold escrows for >N active streams. set streaming_max_escrow=3 per-tenant and fall back to stream_quota accounting.

Sam T: agree. Also include a fast path for diagnostic mode: admins can atomically drain all escrows on an instance for emergency maintenance.

Lina (SRE): I'll draft alerts and runbook steps for: high uncommitted_escrow, eviction_rate spike, protected_reservation_fill.

Joel K: thanks. I'll fold this into the RFC along with API shapes and event fields (escrow_id, escrow_audit_id, commit_mode). scheduling a follow-up sync tomorrow 9:30.

Priya R: add me.

Sam T: on calendar.
